title: Private deployment: SSO federation rollout + crypto accountability and acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Patel
description: PRD fragment and scope clarifications for adding first-class SSO federation support (SAML/OIDC) to Redwood Private, plus mandatory cryptographic accountability features (customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM, key escrow procedures, audit log immutability). This ticket captures the acceptance criteria, test matrix, scope changes from the hosted-only design, and the sign-off checklist for release readiness. Target customers: enterprises requiring VPC/on-prem deployments with strict identity and keying controls.
scope_changes: Originally scoped: SAML SSO for hosted accounts only. New scope: SAML and OIDC federation for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem), including SCIM for group sync as optional beta.
Originally scoped: Basic KMS wrapping for secrets. New scope: full envelope encryption support for model keys and optional HSM-backed signing for audit log integrity.
Add: RBAC role mapping that can be driven by IdP groups and mapped to Redwood roles at the console and API layer.
Add: Streaming immutable audit log export to customer-owned storage (S3/GCS/HTTP sink) and retention controls configurable by tenant admin.
acceptance_criteria: IdP federation: Redwood Private must successfully complete SAML v2.0 or OIDC federation flows with three common IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, PingFederate) in automated end-to-end tests.
Assertion mapping: SAML attributes / OIDC claims can be mapped to Redwood role names; mappings stored in tenant config and applied at token issuance time.
SCIM sync: optional SCIM v2.0 endpoint available for provisioning users/groups; documented as beta and behind feature flag.
RBAC enforcement: API token scopes and Console UI must enforce mapped roles, with unit and integration tests exercising role-denied paths.

Audit logs: Every auth event (login, token mint, role-change, key-rotation) is emitted to an append-only audit stream with cryptographic digest chaining; export to customer sink validated in integration tests.

KMS integration: Envelope encryption implemented for customer secrets using customer-provided KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Integration tests demonstrate key unwrap/rotate without data loss.
HSM option: HSM-backed signing of audit log checkpoints available for customers that require hardware root-of-trust. Documentation lists supported HSM providers and operational constraints.

Upgrade path: Private deployments must be able to enable federation and KMS integration without losing existing customer configuration; migration acceptance test must show zero-auth disruption for >95% of sessions during enablement.
Rollback: A documented rollback procedure exists and is validated in staging: revert IdP mapping changes within 15 minutes and restore pre-change audit checkpoint state.
Operational metrics: Console shows per-tenant SSO success rate, KMS latency percentiles, and audit-export delivery rate; thresholds set and tested for alerts.
Legal/compliance: Data flows and key custody diagrams reviewed and signed by Legal and Security; any export of PII is called out in the runbook.
signoff_checklist: PM signoff: Product requirements verified against customer asks and prioritized (Maya Patel).
Engineering signoff: Implementation plan and perf impact accepted by Eng Lead (Arjun Singh).
Security signoff: Threat model, KMS/HSM usage, and audit-chain design reviewed (Leah Ramos).
Customer Success signoff: Runbook for onboarding and rollback validated with two pilot accounts (Diego Alvarez).
Legal signoff: Export controls and data processing addendum reviewed for target customers (Priya Chaudhry).
SRE signoff: Alerting, runbooks, and operational playbooks verified in staging (Xin Zhao).
Design signoff: Console UX for IdP config & role mapping reviewed (Daniel Kim).
Documentation: Admin guide, runbooks, and API docs published and linked in release notes.
Beta pilots: 2 paying customers completed pilot and provided written feedback or a signed acceptance email.
Security testing: SAST/DAST passed, two pen-test findings remediated or accepted with compensating controls.
test_matrix_and_validation_steps: End-to-end SAML and OIDC tests with Okta, Azure AD, and Ping across three tenants in staging.
RBAC enforcement tests for 6 role permutations (admin/engineer/audit-only/read-only/devops) with API and Console flows.
KMS key-rotation test: rotate customer KMS key and verify envelope rewrap succeeds for sample secret set (1000 objects) within SLA.
Audit export durability test: simulate sink downtime for 24 hours and verify replay delivery and integrity using chained digests.
HSM signing validation: generate and validate signed audit checkpoints with hardware-backed keys; cross-check with software fallback behavior.
Migration test: enable federation on existing tenant with active sessions and measure auth error rate (target <5%).
Chaos test: simulate certificate rotation failures and ensure safe rollback completes without token leakage.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Support both SAML and OIDC upfront to avoid later migration pain; tradeoff is increased test surface and implementation time.
Decision: SCIM will be delivered as beta behind feature flag to de-risk provisioning integration for early pilots.
Tradeoff: Full automated key escrow for HSM will be deferred to a follow-up cycle; initial HSM offering requires customer operator coordination.
Decision: Use digest-chaining for audit logs rather than full blockchain-style commit to reduce operational complexity while keeping tamper-evidence.
Decision: Defer per-tenant custom retention UI (will default to enterprise policy templates) to reduce release scope.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misconfigured IdP mapping could lock out tenant admins. Mitigation: apply new mappings in staged preview mode and require admin confirmation before making live.
Risk: KMS latency could increase auth path. Mitigation: introduce async rewrap and caching for non-critical tokens, measure and cap latency impact.
Risk: Audit export data leak. Mitigation: encrypt export payloads with customer-held key and require signed delivery endpoints.
Risk: HSM operational complexity for on-prem. Mitigation: document operator steps and offer managed concierge onboarding for early customers.
migration_and_rollback_plan: Preflight: Verify tenant has contactable admin and a recovery user is whitelisted before changes.
Staged rollout: enable federation in canary tenants (1%, 10%, 100%) with automated monitoring checks between stages.
Fallback: If auth error rate exceeds threshold for >10 minutes, automatically revert mapping to previous config and notify SRE and Customer Success.
Rollback validation: After rollback, run synthetic user flows and confirm audit checkpoint hash matches the pre-change state.
notes: We will run two paid pilots (financial services & health vertical) to validate legal/contract constraints before GA.
Security requested an HSM compatibility matrix; Leah to provide by 2026-03-05 (received).
Customer Success recommends including an 'emergency access' escape hatch for tenant admins during early rollouts.
